30767645.Title: Technological features of advanced skin protectants and an examination of the evidence base

abstract.1: Products that provide a protective skin barrier play a vital role in defending the skin against the corrosive effect of bodily fluids, including wound exudate, urine, liquid faeces, stoma output and sweat.
abstract.2: There are many products to choose from, which can be broadly categorised by ingredients.
abstract.3: This article describes the differences in mechanisms of action between barrier products comprising petrolatum and/or zinc oxide, silicone film-forming polymers and cyanoacrylates, and compares the evidence on them.
abstract.4: The literature indicates that all types of barrier product are clinically effective, with little comparative evidence indicating that any one ingredient is more efficacious than another, although film-forming polymers and cyanoacrylates have been found to be easier to apply and more cost-effective.
abstract.5: However, laboratory evidence, albeit limited, indicates that a concentrated cyanoacrylate produced a more substantial and adherent layer on a porcine explant when compared with a diluted cyanoacrylate and was more effective at protecting skin from abrasion and repeated exposure to moisture than a film-forming polymer.
abstract.6: Finally, a silicone-based cream containing micronutrients was found to significantly reduce the incidence of pressure ulceration when used as part of a comprehensive prevention strategy.

adaptation1.1: Products that serve as a barrier to protect the skin are important in defending the skin against chemically damaging effects of bodily fluids, including fluid produced from the healing process, urine, liquid faeces, output from an opening in the body and sweat.
adaptation1.2: Many treatments exist, which can be grouped based on ingredients.
adaptation1.3: This study describes the differences in how barrier products work, including petroleum jelly (Vaseline) and/or zinc oxide, polymers (substances made of very large molecules) that form silicone (type of polymer) film, and cyanoacrylates (group of strong fast-acting adhesives).
adaptation1.4: Studies suggest all barrier products work, with few studies that compare ingredients to show one works better than another. Film-forming polymers and cyanoacrylates are easier to apply and cost less.
adaptation1.5: Limited lab data suggest that a concentrated cyanoacrylate made a more notable layer that stuck more to pig tissue than a less-concentrated cyanoacrylate and protected the skin from rubbing and moisture better than a film-forming polymer.
adaptation1.6: Finally, a silicon-based cream with vitamins and minerals needed by the body in very small amounts significantly reduced bedsore occurrence when used with other approaches.

31237193.Title: Efficacy of a Ceratothoa oestroides Olive Oil Extract in Patients With Chronic Ulcers: A Pilot Study

abstract.1: Chronic wounds unresponsive to existing treatments constitute a serious disease burden.
abstract.2: Factors that contribute to the pathogenesis of chronic ulcers include oxidative stress, comorbid microbial infections, and the type of immune system response.
abstract.3: Preclinically, and in a case study, a formulation containing a Ceratothoa oestroides olive oil extract promoted wound healing.
abstract.4: Patients with chronic venous and pressure ulcers, clinically assessed as being unresponsive to healing agents, were treated for 3 months with an ointment containing the C oestroides extract combined with antibiotic and/or antiseptic agents chosen according to the type of bacterial infection.
abstract.5: Treatment evaluation was performed using the Bates-Jensen criteria with +WoundDesk and MOWA cell phone applications.
abstract.6: After 3 months of treatment, C oestroides resulted in an average decrease of 36% in the Bates-Jensen score of ulcers (P < .000), with the decrease being significant from the first month (P < .007).
abstract.7: The combined use of topically applied antibiotics and antiseptics efficiently controlled microbial ulcer infection and facilitated wound healing.
abstract.8: In relation to other factors such as initial wound size, chronicity appeared to be an important prognostic factor regarding the extent of wound healing.
abstract.9: Future clinical investigations assessing the wound healing efficacy of the C oestroides olive oil extract are warranted.

adaptation1.1: Long-lasting wounds that do not respond to available treatments have serious impacts.
adaptation1.2: Things that determine how bedsores progress include low antioxidant levels, other infections caused by microbes (microorganisms), and the type of immune system response.
adaptation1.3: Before symptoms, and in a detailed study, a mixture containing a Ceratothoa oestroides (fish parasite) olive oil extract increased wound healing.
adaptation1.4: Patients with long-lasting leg ulcers (sores) due to blood flow problems and bedsores, determined by doctors as not responding to healing treatments, were treated for 3 months with an ointment with C oestroides extract combined with antibiotics (kill bacteria) and/or antiseptics (slow bacteria growth) based on type of bacterial infection.
adaptation1.5: We evaluated treatment using a common tool used to track wound healing with two cell phone apps.
adaptation1.6: After 3 months of treatment, C oestroides caused an average score decrease of 36% on a common tool used to track wound healing.
adaptation1.7: Applying both antibiotics and antiseptics controlled ulcer infection by microorganisms and helped wound healing.
adaptation1.8: Compared to things like initial wound size, how long lasting the wound was seemed to be an important factor in predicting how much the wound healed.
adaptation1.9: Future studies looking at how well C oestroides olive oil extract works to heal wounds are needed.

31241491.Title: Topical Nifedipine for the Treatment of Pressure Ulcer: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial

abstract.1: Background: Effect of nifedipine on pressure ulcer (PU) healing has not been evaluated in the human subjects yet.
abstract.2: Study question: In this study, the effect of topical application of nifedipine 3% ointment on PU healing in critically ill patients was investigated.
abstract.3: Study design: This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical.
abstract.4: Measures and outcomes: In this study, 200 patients with stage I or II PU according to 2-digit Stirling Pressure Ulcer Severity Scale were randomized to receive topical nifedipine 3% ointment or placebo twice daily for 14 days.
abstract.5: Changes in the size and stage of the ulcers were considered as primary outcome of the study.
abstract.6: The stage of the ulcers at baseline and on day 7 and day 14 of study was determined by using 2-digit stirling scale.
abstract.7: In addition, the surface area of the wounds was estimated by multiplying width by length.
abstract.8: Results: In total, 83 patients in each group completed the study.
abstract.9: The groups were matched for the baseline stage and size of PUs.
abstract.10: Mean decrease in the stage of PU in the nifedipine group was significantly higher than the placebo group on day 7 (-1.71 vs. -0.16, respectively, P < 0.001) and day 14 (-0.78 vs. -0.09, respectively, P < 0.001).
abstract.11: Furthermore, the mean decrease in the surface area of PU was significantly higher in the nifedipine group compared with the placebo group on day 7 (-1.44 vs. -0.32, respectively, P < 0.001) and day 14 (-2.51 vs. -0.24, respectively, P < 0.001) of study.
abstract.12: Conclusions: Topical application of nifedipine 3% ointment for 14 days significantly improved the healing process of stage I or II PUs in critically ill patients.

adaptation1.1: Scientists have not yet measured the effect of nifedipine, a drug to treat high blood pressure and chest pain, on bedsores in humans.
adaptation1.2: In this study, we looked at the effect of applying nifedipine 3% ointment to the skin on bedsore healing in critically ill patients.
adaptation1.3: This was a medical study involving human participants in which neither side knew who was getting what treatment and ointment with no medicine was given to a control group.
adaptation1.4: In this study, we randomly gave 200 patients with stage I or II, according to a common scoring system to measure the severity of bedsores, nifedipine ointment applied to the skin or ointment with no medicine two times a day for 14 days.
adaptation1.5: The most important outcome was changes in the size and stage of bedsores.
adaptation1.6: We used the bedsore scoring scale to measure bedsore stage at the beginning of the study and on study days 7 and 14.
adaptation1.7: We estimated the surface area of the bedsores by multiplying width by length.
adaptation1.8: In total, 83 patients in each group completed the study.
adaptation1.9: We compared patients with similar bedsore stage and size at the beginning of the study.
adaptation1.10: The group given nifedipine had significantly higher average decrease in bedsore stage than the group not given nifedipine on days 7 and 14.
adaptation1.11: The group given nifedipine had significantly higher average decrease in bedsore surface area than the group not given nifedipine on days 7 and 14.
adaptation1.12: We conclude that nifedipine 3% ointment applied to the skin for 14 days significantly improved the healing process of stage I or II bedsores in critically ill patients.

adaptation2.1: The effect of nifedipine (a common vasodilator medication that widens blood vessels) on pressure ulcers (PU), or bedsores, has not been measured in humans.
adaptation2.2: In this study, the effect of skin-level application of nifedipine 3% ointment on PU healing in very ill patients was investigated.
adaptation2.3: This was a randomized study with a sham treatment group.
adaptation2.4: In this study, 200 patients with mild and moderate PU were randomzed to receive topical nifedipine 3% ointment or dummy treatment twice daily for 14 days.
adaptation2.5: Changes in the size and severity of ulcers were the main measures of the study.
adaptation2.6: The severity of ulcers at baseline, on day 7, and on day 14 of the study was measured.
adaptation2.7: Also, the area of the wounds was estimated by multiplying width by length.
adaptation2.8: In total, 83 patients in each group completed the study.
adaptation2.9: The groups were matched for starting severity and size of PUs.
adaptation2.10: Average decrease in the severity of PU in the nifedipine group was higher than the dummy treatment group on day 7 and day 14.
adaptation2.11: Also, the average decrease in the area of PU was higher in the nifedipine group compared with the sham treatment group on day 7 and 14 of the study.
adaptation2.12: Skin-level application of nifedipine 3% ointment for 14 days improved the healing process of mild or moderate PUs in very ill patients.

34408570.Title: Evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy of active specialistic medical dressings in the treatment of decubitus

abstract.1: Introduction: Treatment of decubitus ulcers is a grave medical problem.
abstract.2: In many cases, it is difficult to cure a pressure ulcer, especially when it is deep and extensive, and prognosis is usually unfavourable.
abstract.3: Treatment of decubitus ulcers requires new specialist dressings, which play an important role in the healing process.
abstract.4: Aim: To evaluate therapeutic efficacy of active specialist medical dressings in the treatment of decubitus.
abstract.5: Material and methods: Research involved 40 patients - 18 (45%) women and 22 (55%) men, suffering from decubitus ulcers of different size and depth, localized in the sacral region, lasting from 1.5 to 30 months.
abstract.6: Patients were randomly assigned to two research groups (20 people each), were treated for 4 weeks with 2 different specialist dressings.
abstract.7: ATRAUMAN Ag, which contains silver ions, was used in the first group, while paraffin gauze of BACTIGRAS type was used in the second group.
abstract.8: An assessment of pressure ulcers' healing progress was done with a planimetric method, which evaluates the wound surface area.
abstract.9: Results: The analysis results showed a significant statistical decrease in an average decubitus ulcer surface area in both research groups: in the first group by 60.2% (p = 0.001), and in the second group by 32.95% (p < 0.001), which speaks in favour of dressings with silver ions as having better therapeutic effectiveness.
abstract.10: Conclusions: Using specialist dressings results in a significant decrease in the decubitus ulcer surface area, depending on the type of dressing and active substances contained within, while silver ions support curative effectiveness of the dressing used.

adaptation1.1: Treatment of bedsores is a serious medical problem.
adaptation1.2: Often, a bedsore is hard to cure, especially when it is deep and covers a large area, and usually has a poor prognosis (plan for recovery).
adaptation1.3: Treating bedsores requires specialized dressings, which play an important role in the healing process.
adaptation1.4: We aim to rate how well active specialized dressings, which promote healing by keeping the wound moist, work to treat bedsores.
adaptation1.5: We looked at 40 patients, 18 (45%) women and 22 (55%) men, with bedsores differing in size and depth, located near the bottom of the spine, lasting from 1.5 to 3.0 months.
adaptation1.6: We randomly assigned patients to two groups of 20 people each and treated them with two different specialist dressings for 4 weeks.
adaptation1.7: We used ATRAUMAN ag, which contains silver ions, in the first group and paraffin (waxy) gauze of BACTIGRAS type in the second group.
adaptation1.8: We measured the progress of bedsore healing by measuring the wound's boundaries, which calculates the surface area.
adaptation1.9: Results showed average bedsore surface area significantly decreased in the first group by 60.2% and in the second group by 32.95%, suggesting dressings with silver ions worked better.
adaptation1.10: We conclude that specialist dressings significantly decrease bedsore surface area, and dressings with silver ions work better than those without.

adaptation2.1: Treating decubitus ulcers (bedsores) is a serious medical problem.
adaptation2.2: In many cases, it is difficult to cure a pressure ulcer or bedsore, especially when it is deep and extensive. Recovery is usually poor.
adaptation2.3: Treating bedsores requires new specialized dressings (e.g., ointments, gauze), which are important for healing.
adaptation2.4: We aim to evaluate the success of active specialized medical dressings for treating bedsores.
adaptation2.5: Research included 40 patients - 18 (45% women) and 22 (55%) men, suffering from bedsores of various size and depth, in the lower back, lasting from 1.5 to 30 months.
adaptation2.6: Patients were randomly split to two groups (20 people each) and treated for 4 weeks with either ATRAUMAN Ag, a dressing with silver, or gauze with paraffin (a waxy substance commonly used for coating and sealing candles and rubbers) from BACTIGRAS.
adaptation2.7: Measuring pressure ulcer healing was done by measuring the wound surface area.
adaptation2.8: The results showed a decrease in average bedsore area in both treatment groups: in the first group by 60.2% and in the second group by 32.95%, which speaks in favour of dressings with silver as better treatments.
adaptation2.9: Using specialized dressings leads to a decrease in bedsore area, depending on the dressing type and substances contained within it. Silver supports the healing properties of the dressing used.

34414933.Title: Effect of Ma Yinglong Shexiang hemorrhoids cream combined with pearl powder on the pain and complications of severe pressure ulcer patients

abstract.1: Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of Ma Yinglong Shexiang Hemorrhoids Cream combined with pearl powder on pain and complications in patients with severe pressure ulcers.
abstract.2: Methods: One hundred seventeen patients with severe pressure ulcers hospitalized and treated in our hospital (January 2019--December 2019) were divided into Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream Group (MY Group), Pearl Powder Group (PP Group), and combination with Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream and Pearl Powder Group (MP group), 39 patients in each group.
abstract.3: There was no significant difference in the general data of patients in MY group, PP group, and MP group.
abstract.4: By analyzing the differences in clinical efficacy, secondary effects, scar incidence, pain, and clinical indicators of patients in the MY group, PP group, and MP group, the effects of Mayinglong Shexiang Hemorrhoid Cream combined with pearl powder in the treatment of pain and complications in patients with severe pressure ulcers were explored.
abstract.5: Results: After treatment, compared with the MY group and the PP group, the MP group had a higher clinical efficacy than the MY group and the PP group.
abstract.6: Compared with MY group and PP group, the healing time, dressing change times, and dressing change time of MP group were better than MY group (P < .05).
abstract.7: After treatment, the VAS score and incidence of secondary effects of the MP group was significantly lower than that of the MY group and PP group (P < .05).
abstract.8: The incidence and area of scar formation in the MP group were lower than those in the MY group and the PP group (P < .05).
abstract.9: Conclusion: Compared with Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream or Pearl Powder, combination of Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream and Pearl Powder are more effective in treating severe pressure ulcer patients, and can significantly reduce the pain in the affected area and reduce the occurrence of complications.

adaptation1.1: We aimed to study the effect of Ma Yinglong Shexiang Hemorrhoids Cream combined with pearl powder on pain and side effects in patients with serious bedsores.
adaptation1.2: We divided 117 patients hospitalized with serious bedsores in our hospital (January 2019-December 2019) into the Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream Group (MY Group), Pearl Powder Group (PP Group), and combination with Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream and Pearl Powder Group (MP group), 39 patients in each group.
adaptation1.3: Patients in the three groups generally were similar.
adaptation1.4: We looked at the effects of Mayinglong Shexiang Hemorrhoid Cream combined with pearl powder in the treatment of pain and side effects in patients with serious bedsores based on differences in how well a treatment works, side effects, scar occurrence, pain, and quality of care of patients in the MY, PP, and MP groups.
adaptation1.5: The MP group treatment worked better than the MY and PP groups.
adaptation1.6: The MP group had better healing time and dressing change times than the MY group.
adaptation1.7: The MP group had a better score on a common scoring tool for pain and fewer side effects than the MY and PP groups.
adaptation1.8: The MP group had less occurrence of scars and smaller scar area than the MY and PP groups.
adaptation1.9: A combination of Ma Yinglong Musk Hemorrhoid Cream and Pearl Powder worked better than either treatment by itself in treating severe bedsore patients, and can significantly reduce pain in the affected area and side effects.

34692658.Title: Zwitterionic Hydrogel Activates Autophagy to Promote Extracellular Matrix Remodeling for Improved Pressure Ulcer Healing

abstract.1: Pressure ulcer (PU) is a worldwide problem that is hard to heal because of its prolonged inflammatory response and impaired ECM deposition caused by local hypoxia and repeated ischemia/reperfusion.
abstract.2: Our previous study discovered that the non-fouling zwitterionic sulfated poly (sulfobetaine methacrylate) (SBMA) hydrogel can improve PU healing with rapid ECM rebuilding.
abstract.3: However, the mechanism of the SBMA hydrogel in promoting ECM rebuilding is unclear.
abstract.4: Therefore, in this work, the impact of the SBMA hydrogel on ECM reconstruction is comprehensively studied, and the underlying mechanism is intensively investigated in a rat PU model.
abstract.5: The in vivo data demonstrate that compared to the PEG hydrogel, the SBMA hydrogel enhances the ECM remolding by the upregulation of fibronectin and laminin expression as well as the inhibition of MMP-2.
abstract.6: Further investigation reveals that the decreased MMP-2 expression of zwitterionic SBMA hydrogel treatment is due to the activation of autophagy through the inhibited PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway and reduced inflammation.
abstract.7: The association of autophagy with ECM remodeling may provide a way in guiding the design of biomaterial-based wound dressing for chronic wound repair.

adaptation1.1: Bedsores are a worldwide problem that is hard to heal because it causes long-lasting inflammation (redness and swelling from fighting an infection) and harms the extracellular matrix (ECM; secreted by cells and surrounds cells in tissues) from not enough oxygen and blood flow.
adaptation1.2: The study we did before found that non-fouling zwitterionic (inner salts to which proteins and bacteria cannot stick) sulfated poly (sulfobetaine methacrylate) (SBMA) hydrogel can improve bedsore healing and quickly rebuild ECM.
adaptation1.3: However, scientists are unsure how SBMA hydrogel rebuilds ECM.
adaptation1.4: In this study, we look at how SBMA hydrogel rebuilds ECM using a rat bedsore model.
adaptation1.5: SMBA hydrogel helps remodel ECM better than PEG hydrogel, another bedsore treatment.
adaptation1.7: The relationship between autophagy (cleaning out of damaged cells) with ECM remodeling may influence the design of wound dressings with substances that interact with biological systems for long-term wound repair.

14703441.Title: Etiological diagnosis of chronic cough with unknown causes

abstract.1: Objective: To explore the spectrum and frequency of causes for chronic cough in Chinese patients.
abstract.2: Methods: 86 patients with chronic cough were enrolled in the study.
abstract.3: The diagnostic procedure was based on the anatomical protocol for diagnosing chronic cough designed by Irwin, and additional cytological assay was performed for sputum induced by hypertonic saline aerosol inhalation.
abstract.4: The efficacy of therapy specific to the diagnosis was evaluated.
abstract.5: Results: Definite diagnosis was made in 77 (89.5%) out of the 86 patients with chronic cough.
abstract.6: The most common causes included cough variant asthma (CVA) (24/86, 27.9%), postnasal drip syndrome (PNDs) (22/86, 25.6%), eosinophilic bronchitis (EB) (13/86, 15.1%), and gastroesophageal reflux (GER) (12/86, 14.0%).
abstract.7: After active management based on the diagnosis, cough improved in 72 patients (93.5%).
abstract.8: Conclusions: In addition to CVA, PNDs and GER, eosinophilic bronchitis is also an important cause of chronic cough.
abstract.9: A positive response to the specific therapy is essential to a definite diagnosis.

adaptation3.1: Researchers studied the causes of chronic cough in Chinese patients.
adaptation3.2: This study included 86 patients with chronic cough.
adaptation3.3: The rules for finding the cause of chronic cough included a test to study cells in sputum, as well as other tests.
adaptation3.4: Researchers also studied how well treatments worked according to the cause (diagnosis).
adaptation3.5: The diagnosis was made in about 90% of the patients.
adaptation3.6: The most common causes included: cough variant asthma (CVA), postnasal drip syndrome (PND), eosinophilic bronchitis (inflammation of airways-EB), and gastroesophageal relux (GER).
adaptation3.7: Cough improved in about 94% of patients after treatment based on the cause.
adaptation3.8: Besides CVA, PNDs, and GER, eosinophilic bronchitis (EB) is also an important cause of chronic cough.
adaptation3.9: A good response to treatment based on the cause is very important to making the correct diagnosis.

15895778.Title: Chronic cough as a sign of laryngeal sensory neuropathy: diagnosis and treatment

abstract.1: Chronic cough is often attributed to reflux, postnasal drip, or asthma.
abstract.2: We present 28 patients who had chronic cough or throat-clearing as a manifestation of sensory neuropathy involving the superior or recurrent laryngeal nerve.
abstract.3: They had been identified as having sudden-onset cough, laryngospasm, or throat-clearing after viral illness, surgery, or an unknown trigger.
abstract.4: Cough and laryngospasm were the most common complaints.
abstract.5: Seventy-one percent of the patients had concomitant superior laryngeal nerve or recurrent laryngeal nerve motor neuropathy documented by laryngeal electromyography or videostroboscopy.
abstract.6: After a negative workup for reflux, asthma, or postnasal drip, these patients were treated with gabapentin at 100 to 900 mg/d.
abstract.7: Symptomatic relief was achieved in 68% of the patients.
abstract.8: Sensory neuropathy of the recurrent laryngeal nerve or superior laryngeal nerve should be considered in the workup for chronic cough or larynx irritability.
abstract.9: Symptomatic management of patients with cough and laryngospasm due to a suspected sensory neuropathy may include the use of antiseizure medications such as gabapentin.

adaptation3.1: Chronic cough is often due to reflux, postnasal drip, or asthma.
adaptation3.2: We studied 28 patients with chronic cough or throat-clearing as a symptom of sensory neuropathy (nerve damage of nerves supplying sensation) to the throat and voice box (larynx). This sensory neuropathy involved the superior or recurrent laryngeal nerves.
adaptation3.3: These patients had sudden-onset cough, muscle spasm of the voice box (laryngospasm), or throat-clearing after viral illness, surgery, or due to an unknown reason.
adaptation3.4: Cough and laryngospasm were the most common complaints.
adaptation3.5: 71% of the patients also had motor neuropathy (nerve damage to the nerves that control the muscles) of the throat. This damage was shown by special tests that measure the function of the larynx and vocal cords.
adaptation3.6: The patients were treated with the drug,  gabapentin (a drug used to treat seizures), if the workup did not show reflux, asthma, or postnasal drip.
adaptation3.7: Relief of the symptoms was achieved in 68% of these patients.
adaptation3.8: Sensory neuropathy of the throat and voice box should be considered in the workup for chronic cough or irritation of the larynx.
adaptation3.9: If doctors suspect that cough and laryngospasm may due to a sensory neuropathy, use of antiseizure drugs such as gabapentin may help with these symptoms.

16677450.Title: Etiology and a diagnostic protocol for patients with chronic cough

abstract.1: Objective: The spectrum and frequency of causes and the diagnostic protocol for chronic cough were explored.
abstract.2: Methods: A total of 194 patients with at least 3 weeks of chronic cough and normal chest radiographs were recruited from the outpatient clinic of Guangzhou Institute of Respiratory Diseases between July 2003 to June 2004.
abstract.3: The causes were investigated using a well-established protocol.
abstract.4: The diagnostic protocol included history inquiring and physical examination, pulmonary function tests, induced sputum cell differentials, 24 h esophageal pH monitoring, CT of the paranasal sinuses or chest, fiberoptic rhinoscopy or bronchoscopy.
abstract.5: The final diagnosis was made based on clinical manifestation, examination findings and a positive response to therapy.
abstract.6: Results: The cause of chronic cough was defined in 95.4% of the patients, with a single cause found in 153 patients (82.7%), and multiple causes in 32 patients (17.3%).
abstract.7: The five most important causes of cough were: eosinophilic bronchitis (n = 51, 22.4%), rhinitis and/or paranasal sinusitis (PNDs, n = 39, 17.1%), cough-variant asthma (n = 31, 13.6%), atopic cough (n = 28, 12.3%), and gastroesophageal reflux (n = 27, 11.8%).
abstract.8: Conclusions: The spectrum and frequency of causes of chronic cough in our study is different from the previous reports in western countries.
abstract.9: Eosinophilic bronchitis and atopic cough are important causes of chronic cough.
abstract.10: A modified diagnostic protocol was established accordingly.

adaptation3.1: Researchers studied the causes of chronic cough using specific rules for making the diagnosis.
adaptation3.2: A total of 194 patients with chronic cough for at least 3 weeks  and normal chest X-rays were included from an outpatient clinic in China.
adaptation3.3: The causes of chronic cough were studied using well established rules.
adaptation3.4: The diagnostic tests included: medical history, physical exam, lung function tests, sputum cell counts, esophagus acid test, CAT scan of sinuses or chest, and looking into the nose or lungs with the endoscope.
adaptation3.5: The final diagnosis of the cause of chronic cough was made based on all of these tests plus how patients responded to treatment.
adaptation3.6: The cause of chronic cough was found in about 95% of patients. About 83% had one cause, about 17% hadmore than one cause.
adaptation3.7: The 5 most important causes of cough were: eosinophilc bronchitis (inflammation of the airways), inflammation of the nose (rhinitis) and/or sinuses (sinusitis), cough variant asthma, allergic cough (atopic cough), and gastroesophageal reflux.
adaptation3.8: In this study in China, the types and amount of occurrences of the causes of chronic cough is different from studies done before in western countries.
adaptation3.9: Eosinophilic bronchitis and atopic cough are important causes of chronic cough.
adaptation3.10: Researchers changed the diagnostic rules for this reason.

16995969.Title: Ice cold carbonated water: a therapy for persistent hyperawareness of pharyngeal mucus and throat clearing

abstract.1: Chronic throat clearing or a feeling of 'something' at the back of the oropharynx or nasopharynx is a common cause for referral to otorhinolaryngology services.
abstract.2: While treatment of an underlying causative condition might be expected to improve these symptoms, in many cases a clear underlying cause is not found.
abstract.3: Currently, there is no recognized treatment which is effective against these troublesome symptoms.
abstract.4: This observational study investigated the effectiveness of a regime of sipping ice cold carbonated water to try to break the vicious cycle of throat clearing.
abstract.5: Seventy-two patients with these symptoms who had previously been advised to use the regime were contacted with a postal questionnaire.
abstract.6: Sixty-three per cent of patients documented an improvement in their symptom severity score.
abstract.7: The most severely and most frequently affected patients had the greatest benefit.
abstract.8: We conclude that the suggested regime can be effective in breaking the vicious cycle of persistent throat-clearing.

adaptation3.1: Chronic throat clearing or a feeling of 'something' at the back of the throat (or nose) is a common cause for referral to ear, nose, and throat dostors.
adaptation3.2: Treatment of the problem causing these symptoms may help. But in many cases the cause is not found.
adaptation3.3: Currently, there is no accepted treatment which is effective against these symptoms.
adaptation3.4: Researchers studied a plan of sipping ice cold sparkling, fizzy (carbonated) water to help stop the cycle of throat-clearing.
adaptation3.5: A questionnaire was mailed to 72 patients that had been told to use this plan.
adaptation3.6: Improvement was seen in the severity of the symptoms in 63% of these patients
adaptation3.7: The greatest improvement was seen in patients who had the worse symptoms and who had them most often.
adaptation3.8: Doctors advise that sipping ice cold carbonated water can help to break the cycle of throat-clearing.

19957775.Title: Diagnostic values of the clinical characteristics of chronic cough

abstract.1: Objective: To evaluate whether the clinical characteristics of chronic cough were helpful in determining its specific causes.
abstract.2: Methods: Patients with chronic cough were evaluated by a validated systematic diagnostic protocol.
abstract.3: The patients with identified single cause were divided into 4 groups accordingly: cough-variant asthma (CVA), upper airway cough syndrome (UACS) or post-nasal drip syndrome (PNDS), eosinophilic bronchitis (EB), gastroesophageal reflux related cough (GERC), and the characteristics of the timing, character, onset and associated manifestations of chronic cough in different causes were compared.
abstract.4: Results: A total of 196 patients met the inclusion criteria, including 55 with EB, 45 with UACS, 50 with CVA and 46 with GERC.
abstract.5: No significant difference was found in age, gender and course among EB, UACS, CVA and GERC.
abstract.6: The incidence of nocturnal cough in CVA was 26.0% (13/44), significantly higher than in EB (9.1% (5/55), chi2 = 5.272, P<0.05), UACS (2.2% (1/45), chi2 = 10.657, P<0.01) and GERC (0% (0/46), chi2 = 13.833, P<0.01).
abstract.7: The specificity of nocturnal cough for CVA was 95.9%.
abstract.8: The sensitivity and specificity of cough associated with meals in GERC was 52.2% (24/46) and 83.3%, and regurgitation associated symptom in GERC were 69.6% (32/46) and 80.0%, which were significantly higher than other groups.
abstract.9: The incidence of postnasal drip, rhinitis associated symptom and case history of nasal diseases in UACS were 66.7% (30/45), 88.9% (40/45) and 82.2% (37/45), and the specificity of them were 89.4%, 65.6% and 63.6% respectively.
abstract.10: Conclusion: The timing character and some associated symptoms of chronic cough are useful in predicting a single cause.

adaptation3.1: Researchers studied whether the signs and symptoms associated with chronic cough were helpful in finding out the disease that caused it.
adaptation3.2: Patients with chronic cough were studied by a specific set of rules in order to make a diagnosis.
adaptation3.3: The signs and symptoms of chronic cough caused by a single disease were compared. These patients were divided into 4 groups: cough-variant asthma (CVA), upper airway cough syndrome (UACS), post-nasal drip syndrome (PNDS), eosinophilic bronchitis (EB), and  gastroesophageal reflux related cough (GERC).

19957776.Title: The spectrum and clinical features of causes for chronic cough

abstract.1: Objective: To explore the spectrum and clinical features of causes for chronic cough.
abstract.2: Methods: A total of 103 patients with at least 8 weeks of chronic cough and normal chest radiographs were recruited from the outpatient clinic of China-Japan Friendship Hospital Department of Respiratory Diseases between Oct 2005 to Feb 2009.
abstract.3: The causes were investigated using a well established protocol according to The Chinese Respiratory Society guidelines for management of cough.
abstract.4: The diagnostic protocol included history inquiring and physical examination, pulmonary function tests, induced sputum cell differentials, 24 h esophageal pH monitoring, CT of the paranasal sinuses or chest, fiberoptic rhinoscopy or bronchoscopy.
abstract.5: The final diagnosis was made based on clinical manifestations, examination findings and a positive response to therapy.
abstract.6: The results were compared with those reported in Guangzhou before.
abstract.7: Results: The cause of chronic cough was defined in 95.1% of the patients, of which 83 patients (83.5%) with a single cause, 32 (13.6%) with 2 causes, and 3 (2.9%) with 3 causes.
abstract.8: The most important causes of cough were: cough variant asthma (CVA) (n = 41, 33.3%), rhinitis and/or sinusitis (n = 30, 24.4%), gastroesophageal reflux (GERC) (n = 25, 20.3%), medicine related (n = 7, 5.7%), eosinophilic bronchitis (EB) (n = 6, 4.9%), atopic (n = 4, 3.3%), and idiopathic (n = 6, 4.9%).
abstract.9: Other causes included pulmonary interstitial fibrosis (n = 2, 1.6%), left heart insufficiency (n = 1, 0.8%) and bronchiectasis (n = 1, 0.8%).
abstract.10: There was more nocturnal cough in CVA (80.9%, 36/41) than in other causes (chi2 = 19.81, P<0.01).
abstract.11: In CVA, 63.4% (26/41) was complicated with atopic rhinitis, 68.3% (28/41) showed seasonal variations, and 67.8% (19/28) aggravated in the autumn.
abstract.12: GERC manifested more day coughs, with 56.0% (14/25) cough associated with taking food and 68.0% (17/25) with reflux symptoms.
abstract.13: There was more productive cough in rhinitis and/or sinusitis (73.3% (22/30) ,chi2 = 24.99, P<0.01).
abstract.14: The percentages of CVA and GERC were significantly higher than those reported in Guangzhou (chi2 value were 9.52 and 4.56 respectively, P<0.01), but those of EB and atopic cough were significantly lower (p values were 17.61 and 7.86 respectively, P<0.01).
abstract.15: Conclusions: The most common causes of chronic cough in our study were CVA, rhinitis and/or sinusitis, GERC, medicine related cough, EB and atopic cough, which were different from previous reports in other cities such as Guangzhou.
abstract.16: The spectrum and clinical features of causes for chronic cough are important in the diagnostic procedure of chronic cough.

20392032.Title: Management of recurrent laryngeal sensory neuropathic symptoms

abstract.1: Objectives: We identify management strategies for the treatment of upper respiratory tract symptoms stemming from dysfunction of the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
abstract.2: Methods: We present a retrospective case series of patients who had symptoms of sensory neuropathy, including persistent dysphonia, laryngospasm, and chronic cough.
abstract.3: The patients were followed for symptomatic improvement after initiation of treatment with a neuromodulator.
abstract.4: Treatment outcome was defined by improvement or resolution of symptoms on a self-reported outcome scale.
abstract.5: Results: Of 12 patients identified, 75% exhibited evidence of motor neuropathy on laryngoscopy and 83% had symptoms related to chronic cough treated with neuromodulator therapy over a mean follow-up of 20.4 months.
abstract.6: The median dose of amitriptyline hydrochloride was 25 mg daily, and that of gabapentin was 300 mg 3 times daily.
abstract.7: The mean time from the initiation of therapy to a complete response was 2 months.
abstract.8: Conclusions: Patients with suspected neuropathy of the recurrent laryngeal nerve frequently respond to neuromodulator therapy.
abstract.9: The addition of reflux precautions and acid suppression therapy is helpful in cases of chronic and recurrent laryngospasm.
abstract.10: Patients with evidence of motor neuropathy appear to have better outcomes with neuromodulator therapy.

abstract.1: Background/aim: To investigate the clinical features and underlying etiologies of chronic cough (CC).
abstract.2: Materials and methods: Five hundred and ten CC patients were enrolled.
abstract.3: The phases, characteristics and associated clinical manifestations of CC among the gastroesophageal reflux cough (GERC), cough-variant asthma (CVA), and upper airway cough syndrome (UACS) groups were compared, and the diagnostic values of each group were evaluated by multiple regression analysis.
abstract.4: Results: In the 510 patients, 404 had CC with single etiology-GERC (n = 175), CVA (n = 134), and UACS (n = 95).
abstract.5: The characteristic features of GERC included gastric acid backflow symptoms such as sour-tasting regurgitation, heartburn, endoscopic esophagitis, poststimulation cough, frequent throat clearing, daytime mono-cough, and feelings of heaviness and pain in the chest.

abstract.7: The typical features of UACS included a history and/or symptoms of rhinitis, retropharyngeal postnasal drip, and wet cough occurring mostly during the daytime.
abstract.8: The diagnostic specificities of above factors were >70%.
abstract.9: Conclusion: The most common causes of CC include GERC, CVA, and UACS, and their diagnosis is based on the characteristics of the underlying disease.

27852303.Title: The effects of Nigella sativa on thyroid function, serum Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) - 1, Nesfatin-1 and anthropometric features in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis: a randomized controlled trial

abstract.1: Background: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is an autoimmune disorder and the most common cause of hypothyroidism.
abstract.2: The use of Nigella sativa, a potent herbal medicine, continues to increase worldwide as an alternative treatment of several chronic diseases including hyperlipidemia, hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
abstract.3: The aim of the current study was to evaluate the effects of Nigella sativa on thyroid function, serum Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) - 1, Nesfatin-1 and anthropometric features in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
abstract.4: Methods: Forty patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, aged between 22 and 50 years old, participated in the trial and were randomly allocated into two groups of intervention and control receiving powdered Nigella sativa or placebo daily for 8 weeks.
abstract.5: Changes in anthropometric variables, dietary intakes, thyroid status, serum VEGF and Nesfatin-1 concentrations after 8 weeks were measured.
abstract.6: Results: Treatment with Nigella sativa significantly reduced body weight and body mass index (BMI).
abstract.7: Serum concentrations of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) and anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies decreased while serum T3 concentrations increased in Nigella sativa-treated group after 8 weeks.
abstract.8: There was a significant reduction in serum VEGF concentrations in intervention group.
abstract.9: None of these changes had been observed in placebo treated group.
abstract.10: In stepwise multiple regression model, changes in waist to hip ratio (WHR) and thyroid hormones were significant predictors of changes in serum VEGF and Nesgfatin-1 values in Nigella sativa treated group (P < 0.05).
abstract.11: Conclusions: Our data showed a potent beneficial effect of powdered Nigella sativa in improving thyroid status and anthropometric variables in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
abstract.12: Moreover, Nigella sativa significantly reduced serum VEGF concentrations in these patients.
abstract.13: Considering observed health- promoting effect of this medicinal plant in ameliorating the disease severity, it can be regarded as a useful therapeutic approach in management of Hashimoto's thyroiditis.

29381251.Title: Current evidence for the treatment of hypothyroidism with levothyroxine/levotriiodothyronine combination therapy versus levothyroxine monotherapy

abstract.1: Objective: Hypothyroidism is relatively common, occurring in approximately 5% of the general US population aged ≥12 years.
abstract.2: Levothyroxine (LT4) monotherapy is the standard of care.
abstract.3: Approximately, 5%-10% of patients who normalise thyroid-stimulating hormone levels with LT4 monotherapy may have persistent symptoms that patients and clinicians may attribute to hypothyroidism.
abstract.4: A long-standing debate in the literature is whether addition of levotriiodothyronine (LT3) to LT4 will ameliorate lingering symptoms.
abstract.5: Here, we explore the evidence for and against LT4/LT3 combination therapy as the optimal approach to treat euthyroid patients with persistent complaints.
abstract.6: Methods: Recent literature indexed on PubMed was searched in March 2017 using the terms "hypothyroid" or "hypothyroidism" and "triiodothyronine combination" or "T3 combination."
abstract.7: Relevant non-review articles published in English during the past 10 years were included and supplemented with articles already known to the authors.
abstract.8: Findings: Current clinical evidence is not sufficiently strong to support LT4/LT3 combination therapy in patients with hypothyroidism.
abstract.9: Polymorphisms in deiodinase genes that encode the enzymes that convert T4 to T3 in the periphery may provide potential mechanisms underlying unsatisfactory treatment results with LT4 monotherapy.
abstract.10: However, results of studies on the effect of LT4/LT3 therapy on clinical symptoms and thyroid-responsive genes have thus far not been conclusive.
abstract.11: Conclusions: Persistent symptoms in patients who are biochemically euthyroid with LT4 monotherapy may be caused by several other conditions unrelated to thyroid function, and their cause should be aggressively investigated by the clinician.

adaptation1.1: Underactive thyroid is relatively common, occurring in about 5% of the general U.S. population 12 years and older.
adaptation1.2: The recommended treatment is a single drug, levothyroxine (LT4 - a common thyroid medication).
adaptation1.3: About 5%-10% of patients who use LT4 alone to regulate thyroid-stimulating hormone levels may have ongoing symptoms that patients and doctors may think are caused by underactive thyroid.
adaptation1.4: Science disagrees as to whether addition of levotriiodothyronine (LT3 - another thryoid medication) to LT4 will improve these ongoing symptoms.
adaptation1.5: We look at whether combining LT4 and LT3 is the best way to treat patients with normal thyroid function but ongoing symptoms.
adaptation1.6: We searched PubMed in March 2017 using the terms "hypothyroid" or "hypothyroidism" and "triiodothyronine combination" or "T3 combination."
adaptation1.7: We looked at English articles in the last 10 years in addition to known articles.
adaptation1.8: We did not find strong proof that combining LT4 and LT3 worked to treat patients with underactive thyroids.
adaptation1.9: Genes that cause less conversion of T4 to T3 may explain unsuccessful treatment with LT4.
adaptation1.10: The benefit of adding LT3 to LT4 treatment is uncertain.
adaptation1.11: Ongoing symptoms in patients with normal thyroid function may be due to other causes. A doctor should determine the cause of the ongoing symptoms.
